doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Max Bennett and Mel Lewis joining Kenton
summary: Max Bennett joined for the concert tour and later settled in L.A.; it was also Mel Lewis's first time with the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: The ones they have you credited for arranging here are Sam Meets the Mambo, Theme and Variations, and then Fearless Finlay, which we discussed earlier. Then the next session is Frank Rosolino‟s session. Let me return to that Stan Kenton date, because Max Bennett is playing bass. It‟s one of the first times I see him credited.
Yeah. He joined on that tour.
I know him because of the L.A. Express, but obviously he had a career at least a couple decades long before that. He seemed to have been a major fixture, a cornerstone of the L.A. scene.
Not then. He was an Easterner then. He had been playing with Herbie Fields, with Rosolino, I think.
Yeah, because he‟s in the band.
And somebody else. Rosolino and Max had been playing . . .

. . . yet. So he came out and joined the band for that concert tour and stayed with the band a little bit into ‟55. I‟m not sure of that, because I wasn‟t with the band then. Then he settled in L.A. That was Mel Lewis‟s first time with the band too.
